question.problem:
Find the $21$st percentile of the random variable $X$ if the probability distribution function of $X$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{21}x,\, & 2\le x\le 5, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The $100p$th percentile of a random variable $X$ is the number ${x}_{p}$ such that

$$
P(X\le {x}_{p})=p.
$$

In our case, we want to find the $21$st percentile, which corresponds to the decimal $p=0.21.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le {x}_{0.21}) & ={\int }_{2}^{{x}_{0.21}}\frac{2}{21}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{21}|}_{2}^{{x}_{0.21}} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{0.21}^{2}}{21}-\frac{4}{21}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $21$st percentile is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}_{0.21}^{2}}{21}-\frac{4}{21} & =0.21 \\ {x}_{0.21}^{2} & =(0.21)(21)+4 \\ {x}_{0.21} & =2.9.\end{aligned}
$$
